title: Antibiotic therapy for cholera patients with severe dehydration, pregnant women, and elderly

variants.action: Give single dose doxycycline 200 mg orally
Give single dose doxycycline 300 mg orally
Alternative: give single dose azithromycin 20 mg/kg orally
Alternative: give single dose azithromycin 11 g orally

recommended_action: Administer doxycycline (preferred) or azithromycin (alternative) as single dose

source.title: Clinical tools for cholera treatment facilities

evidence.passage: Preferred is doxycycline single dose (200 mg for under 12 years, or 300 mg for older children and adults).
Alternative is azithromycin single dose (20 mg/kg for under 12 years, or 11 g for older children and adults).

title: Monitoring during rehydration
recommended_action: Reassess patient every 15–30 minutes; if no signs of dehydration and able to drink, consider discharge.

source.title: Clinical tools for cholera treatment facilities

evidence.passage: Reassess every 15–30 minutes… Has no signs of dehydration AND able to drink AND awake and alert…

title: Severe dehydration
symptoms_or_prerequisites: unable to drink or drinks poorly

requires_all.value: unable to drink or drinks poorly

recommended_action: Admit to facility and follow Plan CC

source.title: Clinical tools for cholera treatment facilities

evidence.passage: Severe  One or more danger signs: • Lethargic or unconscious • Absent or weak pulse • Respiratory distress OR at least 2 of the following: • Sunken eyes • Not able to drink or drinks poorly • Skin pinch goes back very slowly

title: Some dehydration
recommended_action: Admit to facility and follow Plan B

source.title: Clinical tools for cholera treatment facilities

evidence.passage: Some  No danger signs AND at least 2 of the following: • Irritable or restless Sunken eyes • Rapid pulse • Thirsty (drinks eagerly) • Skin pinch goes back slowly

title: No dehydration
recommended_action: Do not admit; follow Plan A

source.title: Clinical tools for cholera treatment facilities

evidence.passage: No  • Awake and alert • Normal pulse • Normal thirst • Eyes not sunken • Skin pinch normal

title: Cholera rehydration – Plan C (children >1 yr and adults)
recommended_action: Administer Ringers lactate 100 mL/kg total volume over 3 hours (initial 30‑minute bolus then remainder over 2½ hours)

medication.name: Ringers lactate
medication.instructions: Give 30 min bolus (≈8 mL/min for 10‑13 kg, ≈10 mL/min for 13‑15 kg, etc.) then the remaining volume over 2½ hours

source.title: Clinical tools for cholera treatment facilities

evidence.passage: Children >1 year old, and adults (plan C is 100mL/kg in 3 hours)

title: Cholera rehydration – Plan C (infants <1 yr)
recommended_action: Administer Ringers lactate 30 mL/kg over 1 hour then 70 mL/kg over 5 hours (total 100 mL/kg)

medication.name: Ringers lactate
medication.instructions: Give 30 mL/kg in the first hour, then 70 mL/kg over the next 5 hours

title: Alternative access for hypoglycaemia when IV not available
recommended_action: If intravenous access cannot be obtained, place 2‑5 mL of 50% dextrose directly into the cheek using a syringe (do not use a needle or spoon)

evidence.passage: If non‑intravenous access, 2‑5 ml 50% dextrose fluid can be placed directly the cheek using a syringe. Do not use a needle or spoon.

title: Discharge education on when to seek care
recommended_action: Ensure patients and caregivers understand that anyone with at least 33 episodes of diarrhoea in 24 hours should seek treatment.

source.title: Clinical tools for cholera treatment facilities

evidence.passage: Ensure patients and their caregivers understand that anyone with at least 33 episodes of diarrhoea in 24 hours should seek treatment.

recommended_action: Ensure all patients and caregivers understand how to prevent cholera before discharge.

title: Provide ORS packets at discharge
recommended_action: Provide at least 4 packets of ORS for all patients discharged to use at home; packets can also be used for family members or neighbours who begin to have diarrhoea.
